BLOOD PRODUCTS: INDICATIONS AND COMPLICATIONS 
 
COSTS 
Packed Red Cells:  
R 2 073 
Fresh Frozen Plasma: 
R 1 658 
Mega-unit Platelets:  
R 12 015 
Crossmatch: 
 
R 922 
Type & Screen:  
R 413 
GENERAL 
•
Consent is required for all blood products! 
•
Blood warming only necessary if  > 2 units to be transfused 
•
Continuous monitoring during transfusion 
•
Specific indications and transfusion triggers decrease mortality & morbidity, and costs 
•
Massive transfusion: Whole blood volume (BV) in 24 hrs, or 50% of BV in 4 hrs. 
                                      (Adult BV approximately 70ml/kg) 
SPECIFIC INDICATIONS 
 
•
PACKED RED CELLS (1 unit à 1.5 rise in Hb; 3% rise in Hkt) 
§
Acute haemorrhage: ±FFPs. Platelets ONLY if massive transfusion protocol or 
specifically indicated. Based on clinical features, lactate, vital signs, amount of 
bleeding, Hb < 10. NB: Normal Hb may be misleading/falsely reassuring in early 
bleeding! Transfuse PRC and FFP 1:1 ratio if > 1 unit PRC required. 
§
Anaemia: Hb < 7; Hb < 10 if there is high risk of myocardial ischaemia, or if clinically 
indicated – syncope, ADHF, severe fatigue due to anaemia.  
NB! Find and treat the underlying cause 
•
FRESH FROZEN PLASMA (15-20ml/kg) 
§
Warfarin overdose: if INR > 1.5 and actively bleeding. Vit K and other management 
as per protocol 
§
Acute haemorrhage: See above 
•
PLATELETS (10ml/kg) – use platelet specific transfusion set 
§
Plt <10 – consider transfusion even if not bleeding.  
Plt <50 and bleeding/invasive procedure to be performed.  
§
Platelet dysfunction and active bleeding – regardless of platelet count.  
§
Massive transfusion protocol - PRC:FFPs:Mega-unit Platelets = 4:4:1  
§
Not usually given in ITP, TTP, HUS. 
•
PROTHROMBIN COMPLEX CONCENTRATE (PCC) (1ml/kg) 
Warfarin overdose; as FFP alternative, reversal of DOACs 
•
CRYOPRECIPITATE (5-10ml/kg):  
DIC, haemophilia, von Willebrand’s Disease, hypofibrinogenaemia (all in consultation with Haematology) 
COMPLICATIONS 
STOP TRANSFUSION IMMEDIATELY! 
MAJORITY ARE MANAGED SUPPORTIVELY 
 
•
ABO mismatch and haemolysis 
Rare, p/w fever, tachycardia, chest pain, shock, DIC 
•
Rh mismatch 
Rh negative females of childbearing age MUST receive Rh 
negative products! 
•
Anaphylaxis à See anaphylaxis protocol 
•
Transfusion-related Acute Lung Injury (TRALI) 
ARDS type non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema, shock. More 
common with FFPs. 
•
Transfusion-associated circulatory overload (TACO)  
Fluid overload; may mimic TRALI. More common in chronic 
anaemia/poor circulatory compliance 
•
Hypothermia  
More common with massive transfusion of cooled products 
•
Electrolyte abnormalities 
Low Calcium/Magnesium/Potassium;lactic acidosis 
•
Infection 
delayed, due to contaminated blood/site 
•
Minor reactions  
Urticaria, pyrexia, tachycardia – exclude more serious 
complications, slow rate of transfusion, provide 
symptomatic relief 
Dr du Plessis/ Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020
